scanNote:
GRAMMAR REFERENCE, 7-BET (122-bet). Yuqorida chapda 'Grammar Reference'.

CHAP USTUN (Present Perfect davomi):
'Irregular Verb'. KO'K JADVAL: Affirmative - Long form: I have bought, you have bought, he has bought, she has bought, it has bought, we have bought, you have bought, they have bought. Short form: I've bought, you've bought, he's bought, she's bought, it's bought, we've bought, you've bought, they've bought. Interrogative: Have I bought? ... Have they bought? Negative - Long form: I have not bought ... they have not bought. Short form: I haven't bought, ... he hasn't bought, ... they haven't bought.
'Form': • We form the present perfect with the auxiliary verb have/has and the past participle of the main verb. • We usually form the past participle of regular verbs by adding -ed to the verb. 'watch - watched' Other verbs have irregular forms. 'buy - bought' • We form questions by putting have/has before the subject pronoun. 'Has he washed the car? Have they travelled by plane?' • We form negations by putting not between have/has and the past participle. 'He has not/hasn't washed the car. They have not/haven't travelled by plane.'

O'NG USTUN:
'Use': • We use the present perfect to talk about an action which started in the past and continues to the present. 'John has lived in Paris for the last three years.' • We also use the present perfect to talk about a past action with a visible result in the present. 'I've broken my arm. (I can't write).' • We can use the present perfect to refer to an experience. 'Have you ever been to Paris?' • We can also use the present perfect for an action which happened at an unstated time in the past. The action is more important than the time. 'I've been to New York three times so far.'
OCh KO'K QUTI: 'Time expressions used with the present perfect: just, already, yet, for, since, ever, never, etc.'
'EVER/NEVER': • We use ever in questions and statements. 'Have you ever visited Prague? Prague is the best city I've ever visited.' • We use never in statements. 'I've never visited America. (=I haven't visited America.)'
'YET/ALREADY': • We use already in positive statements and questions. 'Have you done the washing-up already? Yes, I have. I've already done it.' • We use yet in questions and negatives. 'Have you done the ironing yet? No, I haven't. I haven't done the ironing yet.'
'JUST': 'We use just in statements to show that an action finished only a few minutes earlier. Have you finished your homework yet? Yes, I've just finished it.'
'FOR/SINCE': • We use for to express duration. 'I've worked here for seven years.' • We use since to state a starting point. 'I've worked here since 1992.'

Bet raqami: pastda chapda '122'.

sections.title: Unit 7 - Present Perfect (Irregular, Form, Use)
sections.titleUz: 7-unit - Hozirgi tugallangan zamon (noto'g'ri fe'l, shakl, ishlatilishi)

exercises.instructionEn: Present Perfect - Irregular Verb: I have (I've) bought, he has (he's) bought. Have I bought? I haven't bought. Form: have/has + past participle. Regular: watch - watched. Irregular: buy - bought.
exercises.instructionUz: Hozirgi tugallangan zamon - noto'g'ri fe'l: I have (I've) bought, he has (he's) bought. Have I bought? I haven't bought. Shakli: have/has + 3-shakl. To'g'ri: watch - watched. Noto'g'ri: buy - bought.
exercises.explanationUz:
PRESENT PERFECT - ShAKLI.

  HAVE / HAS + PAST PARTICIPLE
  (fe'lning 3-shakli)


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  3-ShAKL (PAST PARTICIPLE)       ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  TO'G'RI fe'llar: -ED
    watch → watched
    work → worked
  NOTO'G'RI fe'llar: alohida shakl
    buy → bought
    see → seen, go → gone, do → done
    (ro'yxat 128-betda)


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  NOTO'G'RI FE'L BILAN            ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  TASDIQ: I've bought, he's bought
  SO'ROQ: Has he washed the car?
    Have they travelled by plane?
  INKOR: He hasn't washed the car.
    They haven't travelled by
    plane.

  ⚠ 'not' - have/has va 3-shakl
  ORASIDA.


⚠ 'PAST PARTICIPLE':

  = o'tgan zamon sifatdoshi
  (fe'lning 3-shakli).

points.en: Irregular verb: I have bought (I've bought), he has bought (he's bought). Have I bought? Has he bought? I have not bought (I haven't bought), he has not bought (he hasn't bought).
points.uz: Noto'g'ri fe'l: I have bought (I've bought), he has bought (he's bought). Have I bought? Has he bought? I have not bought (I haven't bought), he has not bought (he hasn't bought).

points.en: We form the present perfect with the auxiliary verb have/has and the past participle of the main verb. We usually form the past participle of regular verbs by adding -ed to the verb. watch - watched. Other verbs have irregular forms. buy - bought
points.uz: Hozirgi tugallangan zamonni yordamchi fe'l have/has va asosiy fe'lning 3-shakli bilan yasaymiz. To'g'ri fe'llarning 3-shaklini odatda -ed qo'shib yasaymiz. watch - watched. Boshqa fe'llar noto'g'ri shaklga ega. buy - bought

points.en: We form questions by putting have/has before the subject pronoun. Has he washed the car? Have they travelled by plane? We form negations by putting not between have/has and the past participle. He has not/hasn't washed the car. They have not/haven't travelled by plane.
points.uz: Savollarni have/has ni ega olmoshidan oldin qo'yib yasaymiz. U mashinani yuvdimi? Ular samolyotda sayohat qildimi? Inkorni have/has va 3-shakl orasiga not qo'yib yasaymiz. U mashinani yuvmagan. Ular samolyotda sayohat qilmagan.

exercises.instructionEn: Use of the present perfect. Time expressions: just, already, yet, for, since, ever, never.
exercises.instructionUz: Hozirgi tugallangan zamon ishlatilishi. Vaqt iboralari: just, already, yet, for, since, ever, never.
exercises.explanationUz:
PRESENT PERFECT - IShLATILIShI:

  1 O'tmishda BOShLANIB HOZIRGAChA
    DAVOM etayotgan ish:
    'John HAS LIVED in Paris for
     the last three years.'
    (hali ham yashaydi)

  2 O'tmishdagi ish - HOZIR
    KO'RINADIGAN NATIJA:
    "I'VE BROKEN my arm." (I can't
    write - hozir yoza olmayman)

  3 TAJRIBA (umrda):
    'Have you EVER BEEN to Paris?'

  4 VAQTI NOMA'LUM o'tgan ish - ish
    vaqtdan muhimroq:
    "I'VE BEEN to New York three
     times so far."


⚠ PAST SIMPLE bilan FARQI:

  Present perfect - vaqt AYTILMAYDI
  yoki hozirgacha davom etadi.
  Past simple - ANIQ o'tgan vaqt
  (yesterday, in 1998).
  "I've been to Paris." (qachon -
  muhim emas)
  'I went to Paris last year.'
  (aniq vaqt)


⚠ 'BEEN TO' va 'GONE TO':

  has been to = borib KELGAN
  has gone to = ketgan (hali u
  yerda)


VAQT IBORALARI:
  just, already, yet, for, since,
  ever, never - keyingi qismlarda.


⚠ 'A VISIBLE RESULT':

  = ko'rinadigan natija.


⚠ 'UNSTATED':

  = aytilmagan.


⚠ 'SO FAR':

  = hozirgacha.

points.en: We use the present perfect to talk about an action which started in the past and continues to the present. John has lived in Paris for the last three years.
points.uz: Hozirgi tugallangan zamonni o'tmishda boshlanib hozirgacha davom etayotgan ish haqida gapirish uchun ishlatamiz. John so'nggi uch yildan beri Parijda yashaydi.

points.en: We also use the present perfect to talk about a past action with a visible result in the present. I've broken my arm. (I can't write).
points.uz: Hozirgi tugallangan zamonni hozir ko'rinadigan natijali o'tgan ish haqida gapirish uchun ham ishlatamiz. Qo'limni sindirdim. (Yoza olmayman).

points.en: We can use the present perfect to refer to an experience. Have you ever been to Paris?
points.uz: Hozirgi tugallangan zamonni tajriba haqida gapirish uchun ishlatishimiz mumkin. Parijga borganmisiz?

points.en: We can also use the present perfect for an action which happened at an unstated time in the past. The action is more important than the time. I've been to New York three times so far.
points.uz: Hozirgi tugallangan zamonni o'tmishda vaqti aytilmagan ish uchun ham ishlatishimiz mumkin. Ish vaqtdan muhimroq. Men hozirgacha Nyu-Yorkka uch marta borganman.

points.en: Time expressions used with the present perfect: just, already, yet, for, since, ever, never, etc.
points.uz: Hozirgi tugallangan zamon vaqt iboralari: just, already, yet, for, since, ever, never va h.k.

exercises.explanationUz:
PRESENT PERFECT BILAN KELADIGAN
SO'ZLAR:


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  EVER / NEVER                    ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  EVER = qachondir (savol va
  darakda):
    'Have you EVER visited Prague?'
    "Prague is the best city I've
     EVER visited."
  NEVER = hech qachon (darakda):
    "I've NEVER visited America."
    (= I haven't visited America.)
  ⚠ 'never' bilan inkor YO'Q:
  "I haven't never" ✗.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  ALREADY / YET                   ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  ALREADY = allaqachon (ijobiy va
  savolda), have/has dan KEYIN:
    'Have you done the washing-up
     ALREADY?'
    "I've ALREADY done it."
  YET = hali (savol va inkorda),
  GAP OXIRIDA:
    'Have you done the ironing YET?'
    "I haven't done the ironing
     YET."


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  JUST                            ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  JUST = hozirgina (bir necha
  daqiqa oldin tugagan):
    "I've JUST finished it."
  ⚠ have/has dan KEYIN.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  FOR / SINCE                     ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  FOR + MUDDAT (qancha vaqt):
    "I've worked here FOR seven
     years."
    for two days, for a month, for
    a long time
  SINCE + BOShLANISh NUQTASI
  (qachondan):
    "I've worked here SINCE 1992."
    since Monday, since 9 o'clock,
    since I was a child


⚠ 'THE WASHING-UP':

  = idish yuvish.


⚠ 'THE IRONING':

  = dazmollash.


⚠ 'DURATION':

  = davomiylik.


⚠ 'A STARTING POINT':

  = boshlanish nuqtasi.

points.en: We use ever in questions and statements. Have you ever visited Prague? Prague is the best city I've ever visited. We use never in statements. I've never visited America. (= I haven't visited America.)
points.uz: 'Ever' ni savol va darak gaplarda ishlatamiz. Pragaga borganmisiz? Praga - men borgan eng yaxshi shahar. 'Never' ni darak gaplarda ishlatamiz. Men Amerikaga hech qachon bormaganman. (= Amerikaga bormaganman.)

points.en: We use already in positive statements and questions. Have you done the washing-up already? Yes, I have. I've already done it. We use yet in questions and negatives. Have you done the ironing yet? No, I haven't. I haven't done the ironing yet.
points.uz: 'Already' ni ijobiy darak va savollarda ishlatamiz. Idishlarni allaqachon yuvdingmi? Ha. Allaqachon yuvdim. 'Yet' ni savol va inkorlarda ishlatamiz. Dazmolni hali qildingmi? Yo'q. Dazmolni hali qilmadim.

points.en: We use just in statements to show that an action finished only a few minutes earlier. Have you finished your homework yet? Yes, I've just finished it.
points.uz: 'Just' ni darak gaplarda ish bir necha daqiqa oldin tugaganini ko'rsatish uchun ishlatamiz. Uy vazifangni hali tugatdingmi? Ha, hozirgina tugatdim.

points.en: We use for to express duration. I've worked here for seven years. We use since to state a starting point. I've worked here since 1992.
points.uz: 'For' ni davomiylikni bildirish uchun ishlatamiz. Men bu yerda yetti yildan beri ishlayman. 'Since' ni boshlanish nuqtasini aytish uchun ishlatamiz. Men bu yerda 1992 yildan beri ishlayman.

patterns.exampleEn: Have you ever been to Paris?

patterns.formula: I've already + V3. / I haven't + V3 + yet.
patterns.exampleEn: I've already done it. I haven't done the ironing yet.
I've worked here for seven years. I've worked here since 1992.
patterns.exampleUz: Bu yerda yetti yildan beri ishlayman. Bu yerda 1992 yildan beri ishlayman.
